question.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(5),$ calculate $P(\frac{2}{5}<X\le 1).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(5).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}5{e}^{-5x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(\frac{2}{5}<X\le 1)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\frac{2}{5}<X\le 1) & ={\int }_{2/5}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2/5}^{1}5{e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-5x}{|}_{2/5}^{1} \\  & =-{e}^{-5}+{e}^{-2} \\  & ≈0.1286\end{aligned}
$$
